newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 falls sharply at fixing.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 falls sharply at fixing.

text.p: Czech shares fell sharply at Monday's price fixing led by major issues.
Komercni Banka led the way with a 57 crown, 2.9 percent, fall to 1,850, closely followed by power utility CEZ which dropped 26 crowns or 2.8 percent to 901.

SPT Telecom fell 55 crowns, 1.6 percent, to 3,360 and Ceska Sporitelna fell six crowns, 2.0 percent, to 293. Referring to the strong performance of SPT Telecom at the end of last week, Radim Bajgar, a dealer at ING barings said the decline was probably nothing more than a correction.
"Basically it is no wonder the PX50 was down because last week it was quite exceptional. This week passivity of the capital markets reappeared," he said.
SPT Telecom is the most heavily weighted Czech share accounting for 19.7 percent of the PX50's capitalisation. It therefore has an important influence on the direction of the market as a whole.
